mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue to stabilize near their current depressed levels instead of falling further, routine weekday trips should slowly normalize and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean for the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT holding within 2 points of their t-0w levels.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in RESIDENTIAL combined with a drop in TRANSIT suppresses discretionary out-of-home shopping, so RETAIL_REC falls within one to two weeks after the mobility split widens.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 3 and TRANSIT stays below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays above 3 and TRANSIT stays below -25 for at least one full week.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS from a very negative level signals improved outside-home activity and foot traffic substitution, which should raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks when PARKS moves up sharply from its recent trough.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by at least 6 points from the prior weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days after PARKS rises by 6 points or more week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT remains below WORKPLACES by a wide margin, access friction is the binding constraint on shopping trips; the gap predicts lower RETAIL_REC within one week because people are not translating work travel into retail visits.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT is at least 20 points below WORKPLACES
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the next 7 days when TRANSIT is at least 20 points below WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: In a holiday-like demand regime, simultaneous improvement in GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS reflects broader local activity that spills over into retail outings, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week average within 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both improving from t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in RESIDENTIAL implies more time spent at home and fewer discretionary trips, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks if RESIDENTIAL continues edging upward from the current positive baseline.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 3 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL remains above 3 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals a return of dense weekday movement, and that combined rebound should lift retail visits after a short lag of about two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next 14 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Under mobility restrictions, a widening negative gap between TRANSIT and PARKS indicates fewer cross-town discretionary trips and weaker retail demand, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next four weeks if transit remains suppressed while park mobility drops back.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -28 and PARKS falls below -15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite TRANSIT staying below -28 and PARKS staying below -15.
